title: "Read and compare Crop Report tables"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Read and compare Crop Report tables}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

The Crop Report reader turns national and state workbooks into semantic
observations. This article is for users who need to choose a workbook role,
inspect source-reported rows, and then apply the package's canonical
precedence policy. The examples use the package's small, package-owned
synthetic workbook fixtures. They exercise real parser paths, but their
values are not official ABARES observations.

## Read a national workbook offline

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE
)

library(readagau)

fixture <- function(...) {
  path <- system.file("fixtures", ..., package = "readagau")
  stopifnot(nzchar(path))
  path
}

national_path <- fixture("workbooks", "crop-national.xlsx")
state_path <- fixture("workbooks", "crop-state.xlsx")
cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0("readagau-crop-vignette-", Sys.getpid()))
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

Pass a named local path when the role is known. `assets = "national"`
prevents the reader from inferring a second workbook role, and a temporary
cache keeps this reproducible example out of the user's project and home
directories.

```{r national-reported}
national_reported <- read_crop_report(
  c(national = national_path),
  assets = "national",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

validation <- validate_agau_release(national_reported)
stopifnot(
  inherits(national_reported, "crop_report_data"),
  "agau_data" %in% class(national_reported),
  isTRUE(validation$valid)
)

data.frame(
  class = class(national_reported)[1L],
  observations = nrow(national_reported),
  tables = length(unique(national_reported$table_id)),
  valid = validation$valid
)
```

The main reader returns a tibble with the product-specific
`crop_report_data` class and the shared `agau_data` class. Each row retains
semantic dimensions (`table_id`, `geography`, `commodity`, `concept`, and
`period`) alongside values and provenance. A compact view of the contract is:

```{r national-contract}
knitr::kable(utils::head(
  national_reported[c(
    "table_id", "table_title", "geography", "commodity", "concept",
    "period", "period_status", "unit", "value", "raw_value"
  )],
  6L
))
```

## Local identity and provenance

When no official identity is supplied, a local file receives a
checksum-qualified identity. The package does not infer an official release
from a filename or modification time. This is the safe default for a local
workbook:

```{r local-identity}
release_identity <- data.frame(
  release_id = unique(national_reported$release_id),
  release_date = as.character(unique(national_reported$release_date)),
  source_asset = unique(national_reported$source_asset),
  sha256 = unique(national_reported$sha256),
  parser_version = unique(national_reported$parser_version),
  row.names = NULL
)
stopifnot(
  nrow(release_identity) == 1L,
  startsWith(release_identity$release_id, "local-"),
  is.na(national_reported$release_date[1L]),
  grepl("^[a-f0-9]{64}$", release_identity$sha256)
)
knitr::kable(release_identity)
```

For a reviewed official local copy, supply both `release_id` and
`release_date`; supplying only one is rejected. Keep the source hash and
parser version with downstream results so that a later source or parser change
can be audited.

## Reported versus canonical rows

`view = "reported"` preserves every admitted source row. `view =
"canonical"` applies the versioned precedence policy and marks the retained
rows with `record_role = "canonical"`. Canonicalisation does not discard
semantic dimensions in order to force unrelated rows together; an ambiguous
equal-priority collision raises a typed validation error.

```{r crop-views}
national_canonical <- read_crop_report(
  c(national = national_path),
  assets = "national",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
stopifnot(
  inherits(national_canonical, "crop_report_data"),
  all(national_canonical$record_role == "canonical")
)

data.frame(
  view = c("reported", "canonical"),
  observations = c(nrow(national_reported), nrow(national_canonical)),
  tables = c(
    length(unique(national_reported$table_id)),
    length(unique(national_canonical$table_id))
  )
)
```

Use the reported view for source audits and the canonical view when a
downstream analysis needs one selected observation per semantic key. Inspect
the same fields in either view:

```{r canonical-preview}
knitr::kable(utils::head(
  national_canonical[c(
    "table_id", "geography", "commodity", "concept", "period",
    "period_status", "value", "record_role"
  )],
  6L
))
```

## Add the state workbook

The state workbook has its own physical dataset and geography dimension. Read
it separately when you need state detail; do not assume that a national sheet
is a substitute for a state sheet.

```{r state-workbook}
state <- read_crop_report(
  c(state = state_path),
  assets = "state",
  view = "canonical",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
stopifnot(
  inherits(state, "crop_report_data"),
  all(state$source_dataset == "crop_report_state")
)

state_preview <- state[
  state$geography == "Australia" & state$commodity == "Wheat",
  c("table_id", "geography", "commodity", "concept", "period", "value"),
  drop = FALSE
]
knitr::kable(utils::head(state_preview, 6L))
```

## Discover table families without parsing a release

The checked-in source catalogue describes admitted table families and parser
profiles. It is metadata about the source model, not a substitute for reading
the workbook.

```{r table-catalogue}
catalogue <- agau_source_catalog()
crop_tables <- catalogue[
  catalogue$product == "crop_report" &
    catalogue$dataset == "crop_report_national",
  c("table_id", "source_label", "semantic_family", "parser_family",
    "admission_status"),
  drop = FALSE
]
knitr::kable(utils::head(crop_tables, 8L))
```

Period-status suffixes are explicit. For example, `s`, `f`, and `z` retain
estimate, forecast, and projection status while an unsuffixed period remains
`published-unclassified`:

```{r status-contract}
knitr::kable(agau_status(c("2025-26s", "2026-27f", "2030-31z", "2024-25")))
```

## Working with live releases

The local examples above are deliberately offline. For an online workflow,
use an exact supported release ID from `list_agau_releases()` and let
`read_crop_report()` download and cache its selected asset. `"latest"` is
convenient for exploration but is not a reproducible analysis identifier.
Network access is not required when a complete exact cache hit or a local path
is available.

```{r release-list, eval = TRUE}
releases <- list_agau_releases(
  products = "crop_report",
  refresh = FALSE,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
knitr::kable(releases[seq_len(min(6L, nrow(releases))), c(
  "release_id", "release_date", "support_status", "unsupported_reason"
)])
```

When publishing results, retain the release ID, source URL, SHA-256,
`parser_version`, and the relevant attribution guidance. Package code and
package-owned synthetic fixtures are licensed under MIT, copyright Chartwell Macro;
upstream source data, marks, excluded government material, and third-party
content retain their own terms.
